newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by active hog marketings on Tuesday, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen ranging from $47.50 to $48.50 and Illinois top prices at plant could span $47.50 to $48.00, sources there said.
Hogs at Indiana/Ohio plants were seen at $47.00 to $47.50.
Cash hog prices also were seen pressured by a lack of active pork demand so far this week, dealers said.

Fresh ham prices at midday were quoted steady to $2.00 per cwt lower, lean trimmings $1.00 to $2.00 lower and pork bellies were up $1.00 to $2.00, USDA reported. There were 42 loads of pork and two loads of trimmed, processed pork sold.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog movement on Monday totaled 109,000 head, above the estimate of 105,000.
Tuesday's run was estimated at 105,000, compared with 106,000 a week ago and 96,000 a year ago. However, some cash hog sources said marketings on Tuesday likely exceeded the estimate.
